note: Canonical viewpoints. Binding on the world builder: every slot below MUST resolve to a real, framed shot. Anchors are registered by the game via __HARNESS.listAnchors(); explicit poses are the fallback so the set works before anchors exist. Changing a pose invalidates cross-wave comparison — amend, never edit in place.

viewpoints.note: Long-range exterior vista: draw distance, fog, aerial perspective, silhouette layering.
Camera pitched up so the frame is >85% sky. Sole input to the sky-gradient smoothness / banding metric.
Under dense Hist canopy: dappled light, foliage alpha, contact shadows, depth complexity.

Eye-height street view in the flagship settlement: architecture legibility, prop density, NPC placement. W1-GIVER-PRESENCE: this pointed at `settlement_primary_street` with a camera hardcoded at [4,1.7,-6] — the WORLD ORIGIN — while Thorn stands at [3820,13.31,859], so the one viewpoint named for settlements rendered empty terrain and sky and was cited as evidence of a settlement. Repointed at `town-thorn`, which stands in the town and populates it from its own records. W1-04 r4: MOVED, and this is the second time this viewpoint has had to be moved for the same reason — it was a pose chosen before the thing it photographs existed. The round-3 critic photographed the declared pose [3825.5, 15.1, 879] with Thorn's 15 buildings in the scene graph and got a near-black frame: exterior.js#insideBuilding puts that point inside thorn-sapwell's footprint, so the viewpoint named for streets was standing in a shopfront. The new pose is surveyed, not guessed, by tools/world/w1-04-r4-vp04.mjs against the SAME planSettlement() the renderer builds from: [3859, _, 860] is 9.6 m clear of every wall in the drawn plan and has all 15 of Thorn's buildings inside a 60-degree cone toward the town centre, nearest facade 20.4 m. Cross-wave comparisons that cite the old pose must say so; the old pose is preserved in this note for exactly that reason.
Enclosed interior lit by a single warm source: local contrast, shadow falloff, no flat ambient wash.
Standing water at grazing angle: reflection, refraction, shoreline blend, specular.
Framed head-and-shoulders of a named NPC: silhouette, material response, texel density.
Half-metre from a wall/ground material junction: normal/roughness detail, tiling visibility.
Same pose as VP01 at night. Tests that night is dark-but-readable, not a blue filter over day.
Same pose as VP01 in the region's signature bad weather.
Interior ruin/dungeon with minimal light. Legibility floor: the player must still be able to navigate.
Gameplay camera, locked on, mid-fight framing at STRIKE band. Judged for readability of the enemy's tell, not beauty.

RI-MAG05 §B3 requests this viewpoint BY NAME: the HEAVY release frame (startup+1), gameplay camera transform, HUD off, fixed weather and time of day. M2 (local RMS contrast on a 256 px crop centred on the spell core), M5 (spectral slope on the smoke/spore crop), M8 (the flat-shading delta against the same viewpoint with no spell active) and M9 (tonemap response on the core) are all measured here, and so are VFX-SOFT and VFX-LIT.

THE BACK IS THE FRONT. Seam S18 puts the camera behind the character 100% of the time, so the back of the head, the back of the armour, the backs of the legs and the hanging scabbard get more screen-time than any other surface in the game. RI-CAM07 M1, added by amendment (HARNESS.md §6: viewpoints may be ADDED; poses are append-only and nothing above this entry was touched). RI-CAM07's Comparison method M1 opens by instructing that these two slots be added, and until they existed M1, M2 and M4 were unrunnable by construction — the item's own harness-dependency note scores them 0, fail-closed. Pose per §B: arm 2.5 m, pitch −10°, look at mid-torso. The declared pos/look assume the player standing at the arena_flat origin with yaw 0 (forward = +Z), which the setup teleport establishes; tools/render/cam07-back.mjs computes the equivalent pose from the live rig when the player is elsewhere and is the canonical capture tool for these two.

The same pose orbited 180°. It exists ONLY as §B1's denominator: §B1 is a PARITY test (HFR_back ≥ 0.85 × HFR_front), so the front capture is a reference for the back and is not itself a subject.
